summary: Derived-parallels selection is gated by a threshold calibrated on a different frame: min_grade=-4.415 is the (query,chunk) EDGE_RERANK operating point, applied to (concept-definition,chunk) grading, and it silently drops whole works

analysis.author: Hermes Agent
analysis.content:
Found 2026-08-14 while ratifying the cutover at the golden-query gate (todo:9097deed). The gate itself came back 271/272 and its one failure is unrelated to edges; the damage showed up beside it, in panel coverage. Full record: docs/summary/derived-parallels-cutover-2026-08-14.md.

THE DEFECT. scripts/derive_parallels.py gates panel construction on config[scoring].min_grade = -4.415. That number is the thin scorer's calibrated EDGE_RERANK operating point, and the rellm prototype says so in its own flag help: "--min-grade ... min-leg grade floor (default: the student's calibrated EDGE_RERANK threshold)".

Everything rellm validated about that number is on the (query, chunk) frame:
  - thin-scorer-spec.md: "A (query, chunk) relevance cross-encoder"; pairs built ~30/query from a real query distribution; cache keyed by sha256(query).
  - query-scorer-rungs.md: inter-grader kappa +0.800, reproduced at +0.868; the ship gate, the AUC figures and the operating point all sit on that frame.

derive_parallels substitutes a CONCEPT DEFINITION for the query. Concept definitions are abstract descriptive prose, not questions; the input distribution is different and the operating point was never re-derived for it. Nothing in derived-parallels-proposal.md flags this — its "known prototype flaws to fix before adoption" lists only two, both about ranking (min-leg clamping, via round-robin), and the guru port fixed both faithfully. The frame substitution went unexamined by the proposal, the port, and PR #64 review alike.

HOW IT BITES, AND WHY IT TAKES WHOLE WORKS. min_grade is applied TWICE in build_panels:
  1. the anchor gate -- `vias = [c for c in concepts if score[(c,ch)] >= min_grade]` -- a chunk must clear the floor on its OWN score for a concept to contribute any partners at all;
  2. the partner filter -- a candidate partner must clear the floor on that concept.
The anchor gate is the one that darkens whole texts: a work whose chunks all score under the floor produces no vias, so it emits nothing no matter how good its potential partners are. That is why enuma-elish went 249 Pass C edges -> 0.

MEASURED IMPACT (corpus v54): chunks with any panel 3,525 -> 2,427; texts with any panel 201/241 -> 169/241; 52 texts fully dark. 69 of 235 works have their best (concept, chunk) pair under the floor.

EVIDENCE THE FLOOR, NOT THE MODEL, IS WRONG. The scorer's RANKING is right where spot-checked: sunyata_emptiness tops the Diamond Sutra (-3.88), wu_wei tops the Tao Te Ching (-0.09), sephirot tops the Lesser Holy Assembly (-5.12), ritual_fire tops Yasna 43. Only the absolute values sit low, and they track passage length -- chunks under 500 chars clear the floor 12% of the time against 58% for 2,000-2,400 chars. Raw cross-encoder logits scale with how much corroborating evidence a passage carries, so one global cut across lengths penalises verse and aphorism traditions against discursive prose. Caveat: length correlates with register too, so that gradient is not purely artifact -- the counter-evidence that it is partly artifact is wu_wei scoring -0.09 on 700-char Tao Te Ching chunks, i.e. short text CAN score high on a strong match.

NOT EVERY DARK WORK IS THIS BUG. enuma-elish is separately and genuinely mis-tagged (todo:743ba79b): concept.cosmogony exists, is applied to 20 texts across 10 traditions, and was never proposed for it; its best match is theurgy at -4.84 and the scorer is right to say so. That distinction is the sharp edge of this ticket -- a naive "drop the floor" or "pure top-k" fix would resurrect enuma-elish with panels annotated "Shared concept: Theurgy. (derived)" on a Babylonian creation epic, which is worse than an empty strip. Any fix here must leave a mis-tagged work empty.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE. Selection reflects a rule validated on the frame it actually runs on, evaluated against the evidence the approach was sold on (21 of 24 judged strict-relevant partners reachable) and against coverage, with a re-derive proving both restored coverage and continued exclusion of mis-tagged works.
